facts.statement: A farmer discovered the remains of an ankylosaur at a construction site in Jinyun County, China, in June 2008.
facts.quote: In June 2008, farmer Li Meiyun on a construction site at Huzhen in Jinyun County discovered the remains of an ankylosaur.

facts.statement: The species Jinyunpelta sinensis was formally named and described in 2018 by a team of six researchers.
facts.quote: In 2018, the type species Jinyunpelta sinensis was named and described by Zheng Wenjie, Jin Xingsheng, Yoichi Azuma, Wang Qiongying, Kazunori Miyata and Xu Xing.

facts.statement: Jinyunpelta lived approximately 100 to 95 million years ago, during the Albian to Cenomanian stages of the Cretaceous.
facts.quote: que vivó a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 100 a 95 millones de años, entre el Albiense y el Cenomaniense

facts.statement: The holotype specimen dates to about one hundred million years ago, from the Albian-Cenomanian layers of the Liangtoutang Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype, ZMNH M8960, was found in a layer of the Liangtoutang Formation dating from the Albian-Cenomanian, about one hundred million years old.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial skeleton featuring a complete skull but missing most hindlimbs, except for the right humerus and left thighbone.
facts.quote: It consists of a partial skeleton, with a complete skull, but lacking most of the hindlimbs, apart from the right humerus and the left thighbone.

facts.statement: Jinyunpelta possesses two additional openings behind the nostril, known as C1 and C2, which align with the center of the nostril.
facts.quote: Behind the nostril two additional openings are present, in ankylosaurids named the "C1" and the "C2", which in the case of Jinyunpelta are on a level with the centre of the nostril.

facts.statement: The tail club of Jinyunpelta is hexagonal in top view, with its widest point near the rear edge.
facts.quote: The tail club is hexagonal in top view, with the widest point located near the rear edge.

facts.statement: Jinyunpelta exhibited biphasal jaw movement, an adaptation previously believed to have evolved later in ankylosaurid history.
facts.quote: Jinyunpelta is known to have exhibited biphasal jaw movement, an adaptation that had previously been thought only to have evolved in ankylosaurids during the Campanian.

facts.statement: Jinyunpelta is the most basal ankylosaur known to possess a proper tail club.
facts.quote: This species is the basalmost ankylosaur known to have had a proper tail club.

facts.statement: This species is the most basal ankylosaur known to have possessed a proper tail club.
facts.quote: Esta especie es el anquilosaurio más basal del cual se sabe que poseía una maza caudal propiamente dicha.

facts.statement: In 2018, Jinyunpelta was classified within the subfamily Ankylosaurinae of the family Ankylosauridae.
facts.quote: In 2018, Jinyunpelta was, within the Ankylosauridae, placed in the Ankylosaurinae.

facts.statement: In 2018, Jinyunpelta was placed in the subfamily Ankylosaurinae within the family Ankylosauridae.
facts.quote: En 2018, Jinyunpelta fue, dentro de Ankylosauridae , colocada en Ankylosaurinae.

facts.statement: Jinyunpelta is the oldest and most basal ankylosaurid known to possess a tail club, replacing Pinacosaurus as the earliest known holder of this trait.
facts.quote: It would then furthermore be the oldest and basalmost ankylosaurid that is with certainty known to possess a tail club; previously this had been Pinacosaurus dating from the Campanian.

facts.statement: Jinyunpelta was the southernmost known ankylosaurid in Asia.
facts.quote: Adicionalmente, Jinyunpelta fue la anquilosáuridos conocido más al sur de Asia.

facts.statement: The time range for Jinyunpelta is recorded as the Albian stage, from 113.2 to 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (113.2 to 100.5 million years ago)
